a: Between 9pm and midnight — 60.9% of all 79,621 reports occur at night (8pm–2am). The peak hour is 21:00.
56% of all sightings last under 5 minutes. The median duration is 3 minutes. Only 0.8% last over 4 hours.

q: Which state has the most sightings?
a: California leads in absolute count (8,847 reports). But per capita, WA ranks #1 with 58.6 sightings per 100k people. The top 3 states account for 26% of all US reports.

q: Is the 2012 peak real or just reporting bias?
a: Likely mostly reporting bias. US internet penetration grew from 9% in 1995 to 81% in 2012. After bias correction (normalizing by reporting capability), the pre-2000 years show a much higher relative signal. The bias-corrected peak is around 1999.

q: What fraction involve truly anomalous behavior?
a: Our NLP pipeline found 207 reports (0.3%) explicitly describing physics violations. 2,047 describe instant acceleration. 1,660 describe air-to-water transitions. 77 combine silent + instant acceleration — the hardest to explain conventionally.

q: Are there more sightings near military bases?
a: Our pipeline flagged 1,845 reports (2.3%) with explicit military context (AFB, radar, pilot, intercept). This is a lower bound — it only counts reports where witnesses explicitly mentioned military connection. The true proximity rate is likely higher.

'Light' dominates at 21.8% — but this may reflect witness difficulty in identifying a precise shape at night. Geometric objects (Triangle: 10.4%, Circle/Sphere combined: ~12.5%) are more descriptively specific. Triangle reports tripled from the 1980s to 2000s.
